model.note: Weights of the small assistants of the Photo Labeling page (backend/labeling.py). Written by Dinov3-WhaleID model_fine_tuning/cluster/label_assist.py fit; the collect, run and confidence figures come from the page's catalogue replay (experiments/LOG.md 2026-11-11).

pair.what: P(two safe clusters of one encounter are the same whale): logistic on the sequence model's P, the student embedding cosine per part (max over instance pairs) and the gap between the clusters

eval.note: stack-level top-1 / top-3 inside catalogue encounters, every stack decided on its own (no runs)

boundary.what: P(the focal group changes across a gap between two sightings): logistic on the gap, the boat's displacement (EXIF GPS), its speed and the frames deleted at the gap (holes in the camera's frame counter: the culled marker photos)

blend.what: the similarity of a stack to an animal shown in step 2: a weighted mean, over the parts both show, of three calibrated similarities (each a P(same whale) from a logistic fitted on the val days at the stack-animal level): fluke (best fluke cosine to any stack of the animal), dorsal (best dorsal-fin cosine) and other (best body cosine, best sequence P, shortest gap). The researcher's priority: fluke first, then dorsal, then the rest.

fit.note: stack-animal rows of the val days in the fluke / dorsal / rest order. Alone the model's fluke similarity is its weakest part (pair AUC inside encounters, val: fluke 0.67, dorsal 0.73, body 0.70, link score 0.78): a fluke is what a person is surest of, not what the embedding is.

blend.chosen_on: val days, each scored with the calibration of the two others, first choice right of 276 stacks named: weights 3:2:1 77.2 %, 6:3:1 75.4 %, 1:1:1 76.1 %, fluke-else-dorsal-else-other 72.6 %, the link score 77.9 %; train days (embedding in-sample) 81.7 % against 73.9 % for the link score
blend.new_animal: a low similarity is no sign of a new animal (top similarity below 0.2: new 34-48 % of the time), so a new animal is never proposed by itself

order.what: the order of work in step 2 since 2026-11-12 (the researcher's): the first stack of an encounter is its first animal; the stacks that show a fluke come first, then the stacks with a dorsal fin (both in capture order), then the rest, the stack most similar to some animal first; every stack is held against the animal it is most similar to (blend), a no brings the next most similar one. Runs grow in both directions of the capture order.

before.what: the same days in the earlier orders of work (decisions; looks = animals held against a stack before the answer)

stack_by_stack_capture_order.what: the same days sorted stack by stack in capture order (the order of work before 2026-11-11 evening), simulated on the same stacks: decisions and photo comparisons (looks)

order.note: the page's catalogue replay: encounters as in the catalogue, every stack to the animal the catalogue names, stacks of a run that are another whale taken out. Eval: 542 decisions against 611 (animal by animal) and 556 (capture order).

run.what: stacks next to the head stack in capture order (both directions) that go along with it when their link to the unit so far is at least tau

eval.note: the page's catalogue replay under the stack-by-stack order (forward runs only); under the animal-by-animal order see collect (run_precision)

confidence.what: reliability of the ranking per decision under the stack-by-stack order of work (before 2026-11-11 evening); the thresholds still label the log entries (conf). For the animal-by-animal order see collect.

passer_by.what: a stack that links to none of the encounter's stacks within 5 min (isolation = 1 - best link) may be a passer-by or a group animal seen once; 'farther' = log range above the group's median
passer_by.note: all 28 labelled days (30 passers-by: too few to hold days out); scene / lighting change alone was no better than 2 % precision

collect.what: the animal-by-animal order of work of 2026-11-11 evening, replaced on 2026-11-12 by order (flukes, dorsal fins, the rest); kept for its measured numbers
